open_points.subject: canonical_values.canonical_bytes input representation
open_points.text: “module:surface turns every JSON text a request carries … into its canonical form with canonical_values.canonical_bytes” conflicts with “Inputs: One JSON value” and “refused … [for] a duplicate key.”
open_points.question: Does canonical_bytes receive raw JSON text, a duplicate-preserving parsed representation, or an ordinary parsed value that can no longer reveal duplicate keys?
options: An ordinary parsed JSON value after a separate duplicate-key check
open_points.default_guess: Accept raw JSON text for surface input and parsed values from internal callers, applying the same canonicalization rules to both.

open_points.subject: SpooledFile identity and lookup
open_points.text: M22 says “Substitution: equal facts are the same spooled file,” where its facts include digest, size, media type and disclosure class, while State 5 says “A SpooledFile is named by its producing position alone (SpooledFileKey)” and read_spooled_file omits those facts from its lookup identity.
open_points.question: Is a SpooledFile identified solely by run/node/map/attempt/port/list position, or by all M22 facts including content and class?
options: Producing position for lookup but a separate content-derived identity for equality
open_points.default_guess: Use producing position alone as the identity because the later store and read operations consistently use that key.

open_points.subject: functions.add_trial_case file-fixture input
open_points.text: The operation takes “input values by port, optional expected outputs,” yet authored cases may contain file fixtures and the operation must publish their bytes; no phrase says how those file bytes enter the operation.
open_points.question: What representation supplies bytes for authored file inputs and expected file outputs, and how is it distinguished from the digest/size/media-type facts used only for checks?
options: Inline file bytes in each file-port value
A separate bytes map keyed by port and list index
An existing StoredValue or upload reference
open_points.default_guess: Accept inline bytes with media type for each file fixture, including each element of a many-file port.

open_points.subject: clock.monotonic_deadline result
open_points.text: “Outputs: A monotonic deadline and a way to ask whether it passed.”
open_points.question: What exact object or operations are returned, and precisely when is the deadline considered passed?
options: An opaque deadline with an is_expired operation
A numeric monotonic deadline compared by the caller
open_points.default_guess: Return an opaque deadline object whose expiration predicate becomes true when the monotonic reading is greater than or equal to the deadline.

open_points.subject: store.open_store filesystem checks
open_points.text: The operation enforces a “private directory” and “no symbolic link anywhere,” but neither phrase defines the ownership, permission bits, path scope or traversal to check.
open_points.question: Exactly what makes the data directory private, and which path components and existing descendants must be checked for symbolic links at open time?
options: Kernel-user ownership with no group/other permissions; check the directory and all descendants
Check only store-owned paths and files
Check only objects opened during startup using no-follow semantics
open_points.default_guess: Require kernel-user ownership with no group or other permissions and reject symlinks anywhere inside the data directory, including store-owned subtrees.

open_points.subject: sandbox.probe_sandbox probe execution
open_points.text: “Check at start that bubblewrap is present and one probe execution succeeds.”
open_points.question: What code, inputs, bounds and expected observations constitute the probe, and which sandbox guarantees must it exercise before startup succeeds?
options: A full execute_function call with fixed code, inputs, outputs and bounds
Several probes covering isolation, traps, limits and cleanup
open_points.default_guess: Run one fixed execute_function case through the normal sandbox path, checking its expected output and confirmed cleanup.
